519.title: Fale sobre você / Discuss — Modais de obrigação e conselho no seu trabalho
519.note: Respostas-modelo de nível B1–B2 que o aluno adapta.

items.q: What should a remote team agree on explicitly?
items.a: A remote team should agree on core hours and response times explicitly, because nothing important should be left to chance.

items.q: What must a leader do to make new practices stick?
items.a: A leader must model the behaviour first; if you want the team to log off on time, you have to do it yourself.

items.q: What don't people have to do to be productive remotely?
items.a: People don't have to be online all day to be productive; they should focus on outcomes, not on hours visible online.

items.q: What shouldn't be expected outside working hours?
items.a: You shouldn't expect instant replies outside working hours, and a good team protects everyone's evenings.

items.q: How should you keep a hybrid team connected?
items.a: We should have a short weekly written update and a daily sync, so nobody feels disconnected or out of the loop.

items.q: What advice would you give a new remote manager?
items.a: I would say you ought to set clear boundaries and lead by example, because predictable behaviour builds trust.

items.q: Why do you keep stakeholder updates to one page?
items.a: Stakeholders only need three answers, therefore I keep the update to one page and lead with the outcome, not the detail.

items.q: How do you handle technical complexity when reporting up?
items.a: The architecture is often complex, so I translate it into plain outcomes that non-technical readers can act on.

items.q: How do you explain a slipped milestone?
items.a: We hit an external dependency, so the milestone moved by two weeks, and I explained exactly why before the meeting.

items.q: What do you do when the deadline cannot move?
items.a: The deadline is fixed, therefore we reduced the scope instead of the quality, and the stakeholders agreed.

items.q: How do you make a report land with senior managers?
items.a: Non-technical readers skim, so I lead with the result, flag any risk early, and keep the jargon out.

items.q: How do you report a rising cost?
items.a: Because the cost rose, I explain exactly why first, so the board sees the reason before they see the number.
